routes.title: Sheaf-theoretic Smith theory, parity sheaves and the base change functor for the Satake category
routes.brief: Plan sheaf-theoretic Smith theory and the base change functor it produces on the Satake category. The final theorem is Feng's Theorem 4.20: for H reductive over a separably closed field F of characteristic not p, G = H^p with sigma acting by cyclic rotation, and p a good prime for G-hat, the base change functor BC from normalized parity sheaves on Gr_G with k-coefficients to normalized parity sheaves on Gr_H corresponds, under the two Geometric Satake equivalences Parity^0(Gr_G;k) = Tilt_k(G-hat) and Parity^0(Gr_H;k) = Tilt_k(H-hat) of Mautner-Riche, to restriction Res_BC along the diagonal embedding H-hat into G-hat. Two further final statements are Proposition 3.12, that the Smith operation Psm commutes with proper pushforward for a sigma-equivariant morphism of locally finite type schemes of bounded dimension, and its corollary that T^* RGamma_c(Y;F) = RGamma_c(Y^sigma; Psm F), which is the equivariant localisation theorem of Smith, Borel and Quillen in sheaf-theoretic form. Cover: the constructible and ind-constructible Tate categories, that is the Verdier quotients of the bounded constructible and ind-constructible equivariant derived categories by perfect, respectively flat, complexes over the group ring, with the identification of Flat^b as the objects of locally finite tor-amplitude and with the fact that shift by two is the identity on the Tate category; the Smith operation Psm = T^* i^*, the six operations on Tate categories, the lemmas that pushforward along a free quotient and from a free action land in Flat^b, and that the cone of i^! to i^* is flat; Tate cohomology of complexes and of sheaves by the colimit along the two-periodicity map, with its long exact sequence and its behaviour under a trivial action; parity sheaves after Juteau-Mautner-Williamson, with JMW stratifications, pariversities, the structure of indecomposable parity complexes and the existence of parity sheaves on affine Grassmannians; Tate-parity sheaves after Leslie-Lonergan with integral coefficients, modular reduction, and the lifting functor; tilting modules for the dual group with the theorem that normalized parity sheaves on Gr_G are tilting modules and that tiltings generate the bounded derived category of representations; and finally the norm functor Nm on the Satake category, the proof that Psm preserves parity, the Frobenius twist of a k-linear category, the construction of BC, its additivity, Galois equivariance and exactness, and the reduction to a torus through hyperbolic localisation that proves Theorem 4.20. Import from: Geometric Satake over the Fargues-Fontaine curve (GeometricSatakeAndFusion) for the affine Grassmannian, the Satake category with convolution and the Tannakian dual group, and for semi-infinite geometry and the constant-term functor; Etale duality, cycle classes and perverse sheaves (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves) for the six operations, Verdier duality and the perverse t-structure; Reductive groups, Part II (ReductiveGroupsPartII) for the dual group; and Reductive algebraic groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups) together with the proposed Part II on integral highest weights (ReductiveGroupsIntegralRepresentationsPartII) for Weyl and costandard modules in characteristic p, on which the tilting-module theory rests. Tate cohomology of a finite cyclic group and Witt vectors are already in the libraries and must not be rebuilt.
routes.reason: A search of data/atlas.json for Smith theory, parity sheaves, Tate categories and tilting modules returns nothing: the only Tate cohomology in the atlas is the class-formation layer of the Tau Ceti class field theory roadmap, and the perverse machinery in EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves is about the perverse t-structure, not about a mod 2 parity condition that survives a Verdier quotient in which shift by two is the identity. Nor is there a direction to extend: GeometricSatakeAndFusion plans the Satake category, its convolution and the dual group, but nothing about equivariant localisation for a Z/p-action on it, and the whole point of §§3–4 is a second, exotic localisation of that category. This material is also not specific to base change: sheaf-theoretic Smith theory, parity sheaves and Tate-parity sheaves are general tools of modular representation theory, used by Riche–Williamson for the linkage principle and by Leslie–Lonergan for the Frobenius contraction functor, so a roadmap of their own is the right home and both those papers and this one are sources for it.

routes.title: Global shtukas and Langlands over function fields, Part II: mod p coefficients, Tate cohomology of shtukas and cyclic base change
routes.brief: Plan Tate cohomology of moduli stacks of shtukas with mod p coefficients and the global cyclic base change it produces. The final theorems are Feng's Theorem 5.11 and Theorem 5.13. Theorem 5.11: for X a smooth projective curve over F_ell with ell not p, H reductive over its function field F with a parahoric model, E/F cyclic of degree p and G = Res_{X'/X}(H_{X'}), fix a closed point x_0 and a closed finite subscheme D; then for j in {0,1}, under the isomorphism T^j(Sht_{G,D+infinity x_0, empty};1) = H_c^j(Sht_{H,D+infinity x_0,empty};1) induced by the identification of Sht_H with the sigma-fixed locus of Sht_G, the excursion operator S_{I,Nm^{(1/p)}(V),Nm^{(1/p)}(x),Nm^{(1/p)}(xi), (gamma_i)} of Exc(Gamma,^LG)^sigma acts as S_{I,Res_BC(V),x,xi,(gamma_i)} of Exc(Gamma,^LH), and the operators S_{I,N.V,(N.x) composed with Delta_p, nabla_p composed with (N.xi),(gamma_i)} act as zero. Theorem 5.13: an L-parameter arising from the action of Exc(Gamma,^LH) on H^0_c(Sht_H;Sat(1))_alpha has its image under phi_BC arising from the action of Exc(Gamma,^LG) on H^0_c(Sht_G;Sat(1))_{phi(alpha)}; equivalently, if rho into ^LH(k) is automorphic then phi_BC composed with rho is automorphic, which is strong base change, not merely agreement of unramified Hecke eigensystems. Cover: the base change setup for shtukas and the identification of the shtuka stack for H with the sigma-fixed locus of the one for G on representable truncations; Tate cohomology of moduli of shtukas and of the colimit over Harder-Narasimhan bounds and level at a fixed point, at infinite level; Drinfeld's lemma for Tate cohomology, that is the factorisation of the partial Weil group action through the product of copies of the Weil group, together with the Eichler-Shimura relation of Xue and its Tate cohomology form and the finite-type filtration it needs; the axiomatics of admissible families of functors and the excursion action they carry; the Tate diagonal homomorphism of a commutative algebra in characteristic p, the unique extension of characters it gives, the norm and norm-element formulas in the excursion algebra and the subalgebra Exc' they generate; the Frobenius twist and linearization of algebras; and the functoriality of excursion algebras along an admissible L-homomorphism together with the base change homomorphism phi_BC and the comparison between the algebraic and geometric L-groups that relates the two normalisations. Import from: Global shtukas and Langlands over function fields (GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands) for shtuka stacks with legs, level and truncations, the Satake functor on them, partial Frobenius and Drinfeld's lemma for ordinary cohomology, and the excursion algebra with its reconstruction of semisimple parameters, all of which the parent roadmap plans with ell-adic characteristic-zero coefficients; this Part II is the mod p theory, where finiteness of the cuspidal sector is replaced by Xue's extension to all compactly supported functions. Import also Sheaf-theoretic Smith theory and the base change functor for the Satake category (SheafTheoreticSmithTheory) for the Smith operation, equivariant localisation and the functor BC, and Reductive groups, Part II (ReductiveGroupsPartII) for the dual group and the L-group.
routes.reason: The parent roadmap owns precisely the objects §5 acts on — shtuka stacks with legs, level and truncations (GS.2), their compactly supported cohomology with Hecke and cohomological correspondences (GS.3), partial Frobenius and Drinfeld's lemma (GS.4), and excursion operators with the reconstruction of semisimple L-parameters (GS.5) — and the paper is a source for those layers (see the source route below). What it adds is new layers in the same direction: its stated coefficient field is characteristic-zero ℓ-adic, whereas this whole paper lives in characteristic p, where the Hecke-finite cuspidal sector of GS.3 is replaced by Xue's extension of the excursion action to all compactly supported functions; and, on top of that, a Z/pZ-action on the entire shtuka tower, the identification of Sht_H with its fixed locus, Tate cohomology of shtukas in place of cohomology, Drinfeld's lemma for Tate cohomology, and the resulting identity between excursion operators for G and for H. None of that is planned anywhere. It is a Part II rather than a new roadmap because every statement is about the moduli of shtukas and the excursion action that the parent roadmap constructs.

routes.title: Smooth representations of local groups, Part II: mod p Bernstein centers, the Brauer homomorphism and local cyclic base change
routes.brief: Plan the local theory: mod p Hecke algebras at Moy-Prasad level, the base change homomorphism of Bernstein centers, and local cyclic base change for the Genestier-Lafforgue correspondence. The final theorems are Feng's Theorem 6.21, Theorem 6.26 and Corollary 6.15, under the standing hypothesis that p is an odd good prime for G-hat, with F_v a local function field of residue characteristic ell not p, H reductive over F_v, E_v/F_v cyclic of degree p and G = Res_{E_v/F_v}(H_{E_v}). Theorem 6.21: for an irreducible admissible representation Pi of G(F_v) over k with character chi_{Pi^{(p)}} of the excursion algebra attached to its Frobenius twist, every irreducible character chi of Exc(W_v,^LH) appearing in the action on T^*(Pi) satisfies chi composed with phi_BC^* equal to chi_{Pi^{(p)}}; this is the Treumann-Venkatesh conjecture that Tate cohomology realises functoriality. Theorem 6.26: for every irreducible representation pi of H(F_v) over k with nonzero U_r-fixed vectors there is an irreducible representation Pi of G(F_v) with nonzero K_r-fixed vectors and rho_Pi isomorphic to phi_BC composed with rho_pi, with the depth estimate depth(Pi) at most depth(pi) in the normalisation of Remark 6.27. Corollary 6.15: the square formed by phi_BC^* on excursion algebras, the Genestier-Lafforgue maps Z_G and Z_H, and the homomorphism Z_TV of Bernstein centers commutes. Cover: Hecke algebras H(G,K_r) for K_r the Moy-Prasad filtration subgroups at a point of the Bruhat-Tits building, with k-coefficients, their centers and the Bernstein center as the inverse limit; the injectivity of the map of double coset spaces at a special vertex and the surjectivity of restriction it gives; plain subgroups, the unnormalized Brauer homomorphism and its compatibility with Tate cohomology, and the fact that every subgroup of the pro-ell radical is plain; the Treumann-Venkatesh homomorphism at each level, its compatibility with change of level, and the resulting Z_TV; the Genestier-Lafforgue correspondence through the map Z_G from the excursion algebra to the Bernstein center and its local-global compatibility; linkage of local representations and the Treumann-Venkatesh conjecture; and the finiteness of Hecke algebras over their centers, quoted from Dat-Helm-Kurinczuk-Moss, which together with Nakayama produces the base change representation. Import from: Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups) for the smooth category over arbitrary coefficients, admissibility, Hecke algebras over rings and the Bernstein center; Reductive groups, Part II (ReductiveGroupsPartII) for buildings, parahoric and congruence group schemes and the Cartan decomposition; Global shtukas and Langlands over function fields, Part II (ShtukaTateCohomologyAndGlobalBaseChange) for the global input, namely the identification of excursion operators under equivariant localisation; and Arithmetic locally symmetric spaces and their cohomology, Part II: Smith theory and mod p functoriality (SmithTheoryAndModPFunctoriality), proposed by PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16, which plans the same Brauer homomorphism, plain subgroups, linkage and the conjecture: whichever design job runs first owns those statements and the other imports them rather than planning them again.
routes.reason: Section 6 is local representation theory of p-adic groups with characteristic p coefficients: Hecke algebras at Moy-Prasad level and their centers, the Bernstein center, the Brauer homomorphism, and the Genestier-Lafforgue correspondence. The parent roadmap plans the smooth category over arbitrary coefficients (SR.0), Hecke algebras over rings with the explicit instruction that characteristic p is to be handled in the smooth action category by integral double-coset operators (SR.1), and the Bernstein center, though its SR.3 layer is written for complex coefficients. New layers are needed for: the mod p Bernstein center as an inverse limit over Moy-Prasad levels; the base change homomorphism Z_TV, which Haines sought in characteristic zero and which is constructed here for general groups and arbitrary depth; the Genestier-Lafforgue map from the excursion algebra to the Bernstein center with its local-global compatibility; and the two main local theorems. This is distinct from the Part IIs of the same parent already proposed by other extractions — types and supercuspidals (PAPER-FINTZEN-21), Newton cocenters (PAPER-HE-18), parahoric centers (PAPER-HE-21, PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-18, PAPER-ZHU-17), general-linear newforms (PAPER-ATOBE-KONDO-YASUDA-22) and unitary spherical representations (PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26) — none of which touches characteristic p coefficients or base change. Where it overlaps the Part II of ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces proposed by PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16 — plain subgroups, the unnormalized Brauer homomorphism, its compatibility with Tate cohomology, linkage and the Treumann-Venkatesh conjecture, which are that paper's statements quoted here — the two must not both plan them; the brief says which imports which.

Sections 2 and 5.1 are a careful, self-contained account of exactly what these layers plan, and the paper is a good source for them even though everything it says there is already planned. GS.5 plans excursion operators indexed by invariant functions and Galois tuples with their relations, and the reconstruction of continuous semisimple L-parameters from characters of the excursion algebra: §2 gives the excursion algebra by generators and relations in two presentations — one by invariant functions on G-hat \ (^LG)^I / G-hat, one by a representation with an invariant vector and an invariant functional — together with the comparison between them and Lafforgue's reconstruction theorem in the form proved for modular coefficients by Böckle–Harris–Khare–Thorne. GS.1 and GS.2 plan the global Hecke stack, classical geometric Satake on it, and multi-leg shtukas with bounds, level, partial Frobenius and truncations: §5.1 sets all of that up, including the iterated shtuka stacks and the stratified smallness of the map to Sht_{G,D,I}. GS.4 plans Drinfeld's lemma and the continuous action of a product of global Galois groups, which is the statement Appendix B transports to Tate cohomology. The roadmap is a campaign roadmap, not a Tau Ceti one, so it may take the paper as a source.

review.reason: Confirmed, and I checked it the way the finding says it was found. The two sentences read `Then using Proposition \ref{B: eichler-shimura}, we may eliminate all powers of partial Frobenius with exponent $\geq \dim W$' and `Therefore the Eichler-Shimura relation from Proposition \ref{B: eichler-shimura} is also satisfied in the right column', and the label sits on `\begin{lemma}\label{B: eichler-shimura}'. Rebuilding the paper's thirteen-environment counter from the source confirms the numbering the finding relies on: B.1 is a Proposition (Xue's Eichler–Shimura relation for ordinary cohomology) and B.3 is the Lemma, its Tate-cohomology analogue, which is the statement §B.3 needs. Only the word is wrong.
